title: canary-synthetic-runbook-and-trace-mappings
content:
Status: DRAFT - working notes for on-call + SRE + applied-ML to operate canaries and map traces to dashboard drilldowns.

Purpose:
- Capture a compact, actionable set of metrics definitions, tracing attribute conventions, dashboard layout, and an investigative runbook specific to canary/synthetic traffic for the inference platform.
- Focus: detect model-quality regressions, performance regressions (latency/cost), and platform regressions (resource throttling, KV-cache behavior) using a small set of synthetic tests and tracing signal mappings.

Scope / assumptions:
- Canary traffic runs from the synthetic runner service (svc.synthetic-runner) to target model endpoints.
- Synthetic inputs include: short prompt (chat-lite), long prompt (context-heavy), stream-mode prompt (streaming tokens > 256), and embedding job.
- Metrics emitted via OpenTelemetry -> Prometheus exporter; traces stored in Jaeger.

Key metric naming conventions (single-line defs for dashboard and alerts):
- ri_canary_request_total: counter - total synthetic requests sent (labels: canary_id, test_type, model).
- ri_canary_success_total: counter - synthetic requests that returned 2xx + validation pass (labels).
- ri_canary_validation_failures_total: counter - returned 2xx but validation/syntax mismatch (e.g., missing required key).
- ri_inference_latency_ms_bucket{le,quantile}: histogram - end-to-end server latency for inference (includes queuing, decode).
- ri_token_stream_latency_ms_p50|p95|p99: gauge - token emission latencies for streaming responses (separate series per model).
- ri_kv_cache_hit_ratio: gauge (0..1) - per-model, per-host cache hit ratio for KV/prefix cache (labels: model, shard).
- ri_gpu_utilization_percent: gauge - per-gpu utilization from metrics exporter.
- ri_batch_size_avg: gauge - moving average batch size processed by serving runtime.
- ri_memory_pressure_mb: gauge - host memory RSS for inference process.
- ri_failed_fallback_total: counter - requests that failed primary model and fell back to a compatible variant.
- ri_model_quality_score: gauge - synthetic-runner computed score (0..1) comparing expected tokens/semantics.

Suggested PromQL snippets (for Grafana panels):
- Canary success rate (1m): sum(rate(ri_canary_success_total[1m])) / sum(rate(ri_canary_request_total[1m]))
- Canary validation failure rate (5m): sum(rate(ri_canary_validation_failures_total[5m])) by (test_type) / sum(rate(ri_canary_request_total[5m])) by (test_type)
- P95 latency for long prompt: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ri_inference_latency_ms_bucket{test_type=\"long-prompt\",model=~\".*\"}[5m])) by (le, model))
- KV cache hit ratio per model: avg(ri_kv_cache_hit_ratio) by (model)

Tracing conventions (span / attribute naming to include in code/OT instrumentation):
- Root span name: synthetic.request (attributes: synthetic.canary_id, synthetic.test_type, synthetic.expected_signature)
- Server side child spans: 
  - span: transport.accept (attrs: transport.protocol, client.region)
  - span: routing.resolve (attrs: routed.model, route.rule_id)
  - span: queue.wait (attrs: queue_len, queue_time_ms)
  - span: model.init (attrs: model.name, model.version, init_time_ms, quantized:true|false)
  - span: model.forward (attrs: device:gpu|cpu, gpu.id, batch.size, seq_len, kv_cache_hit_count, kv_cache_miss_count)
  - span: decode.generate (attrs: tokens_emitted, decode.strategy)
  - span: streaming.flush (attrs: flush.size, flush.duration_ms)
  - span: fallback.invoke (attrs: fallback.to_model, fallback.reason)
- Trace-level attributes: trace.synthetic=true, trace.synthetic_priority=low|high, trace.correlation_id (use request id)

Why these attributes matter:
- kv_cache_hit_count + batch.size allow quick root-cause of latency regressions: low batch sizes + many cache misses => more per-token compute.
- route.rule_id lets us link routing changes to sudden model mismatches.
- trace.synthetic_priority distinguishes canary vs real traffic so we don't mistakenly apply user-facing SLOs.

Dashboard layout (panel-by-panel, top -> bottom):
- Row: Canary Overview
  * Metric badges: current canary success rate (1m), validation-fail rate (5m), model_quality_score (1m)
  * Small table: last 50 synthetic requests (cols: time, canary_id, test_type, model, result, trace_link)
- Row: Latency and Token Metrics (split)
  * P50/P95/P99 latency by test_type (stacked lines per model)
  * Token stream p95 by model (compare stream vs non-stream tests)
  * Heatmap: latency distribution by hour for last 72h
- Row: Resource Correlation
  * GPU utilization by shard + batch size trend (overlay GPU util & batch_size_avg)
  * KV cache hit ratio per model (bar chart)
- Row: Traces & Drilldowns
  * Error waterfall: top failing spans aggregated by span.name (count & median duration)
  * Trace sample panel: clickable links that open Jaeger traces filtered by trace.synthetic=true and canary_id=<id>
  * Quick queries: prefilled attributes to jump to traces (e.g., kv_cache_miss_count>0 and model.forward>200ms)
- Row: Canary history + perf regressions
  * Sparkline grid of model_quality_score over past 7 days per model
  * Canary rollout correlation: shows canary start/end annotations and any code deploy tags (linked_artifacts)

Alerting recommendations (examples):
- Canary failure (high-confidence): if 5m success rate < 95% AND validation_fail_rate > 5% -> Sev2 alert.
- Latency regression: per-model P95 increased by > 50% vs 7d baseline and absolute P95 > 1200ms -> Sev2.
- KV cache degradation: drop in ri_kv_cache_hit_ratio by > 30% relative to 1h baseline and concurrent P95 up -> Sev3 with runbook.
- Fallback noise: rate(ri_failed_fallback_total[5m]) > 1/min for > 10 minutes -> paging to oncall if customer-facing canary.

Investigation runbook (first 12 minutes):
1) Confirm the alert and scope: check canary ids involved, models, test_type, top hosts. (Dashboard: Canary Overview -> table)
2) If latency regression: open Trace sample panel -> filter for test_type and model -> look for span duration distribution. Check model.forward spans for batch.size and kv_cache attributes.
3) If model_quality drop: pull the last 20 synthetic inputs and outputs (there's a debug bucket S3 path per canary) and run the local comparator. Check model.version in spans to see if rollout matches canary.
4) Resource checks: look at GPU utilization and host memory pressure. Throttling or eviction events often show as repeated model.init spans (cold starts).
5) If KV cache miss spike: identify hosts with kv_cache_miss_count > threshold and check recent cache eviction logs (k8s events, mem pressure).
6) Correlate with deploys: query linked_artifacts for recent PRs matching route.rule_id or model.version.
7) If necessary, execute mitigation: rollback routing rule, increase dedicated capacity, or disable canary. Use the Console runbook links in dashboard.
Postmortem/next steps guidance:
- Add integration test that reproduces the failing case when we see systemic validation failures.
- If trace sampling missed the problematic requests (low coverage), increase sampling rate for traces where trace.synthetic=true for the next 24 hours.
- Consider adding a light-weight synthetic that exercises the particular token/sequence shape that failed (e.g., repetition boundary).

Instrumentation TODOs (developer checklist):
- [ ] Ensure synthetic.runner sets trace.synthetic=true and synthetic.canary_id for every canary request.
- [ ] Emit ri_canary_validation_failures_total with reason label (e.g., schema_mismatch, hallucination_keyword).
- [ ] Model runtime: expose kv_cache_hit_count and kv_cache_miss_count as attributes on model.forward span.
- [ ] Add model.version and route.rule_id to routing.resolve span.
- [ ] Add a compact trace link field to request logs: trace_link=https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/{{trace_id}}

Notes / open questions:
- How to surface streaming token anomalies (e.g., long pauses) in an aggregated way? Proposal: compute ri_token_stream_gap_count for gaps>250ms per stream session.
- Should canary alerts be auto-silenced outside business hours? Some canaries are low-priority. Need a per-canary priority label.

Linked artifacts / references:
- Jira: JIRA-INF-2142 (canary-runner enhancements), JIRA-OBS-78 (kv-cache metrics)
